title: ADD --keep-git-dir=false is silently accepted and ignored; .git is copied anyway
body:
## Description

`ADD --keep-git-dir` has three spellings, and buildah handles them inconsistently:

| Form | imagebuilder parses to | buildah does | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--keep-git-dir` | `true` | hard error | ✅ honest — user knows it's unsupported |
| `--keep-git-dir=true` | `true` | hard error | ✅ honest |
| `--keep-git-dir=false` | `false` | **nothing** | ❌ **silently wrong** |

In the third case the user is explicitly asking for the `.git` directory to be **excluded**
from the image. Buildah accepts the flag without complaint and then copies `.git` in anyway —
delivering the exact opposite of what was requested, with no error and no warning.

This matters beyond tidiness: `.git` in a build context can carry remote URLs with embedded
credentials, full history, and prior versions of files that were deliberately removed.
Silently shipping it into an image layer is a plausible way to leak secrets.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Write three Containerfiles differing only in the `--keep-git-dir` spelling:

```console
$ printf 'FROM scratch\nADD --keep-git-dir=true  https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World.git /src\n' > Cf.keeptrue
$ printf 'FROM scratch\nADD --keep-git-dir=false https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World.git /src\n' > Cf.keepfalse
$ printf 'FROM scratch\nADD                      https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World.git /src\n' > Cf.keepnone
```

2. Build each, then check whether `.git` made it into the image.

## Describe the results you received

`=true` errors as expected. `=false` **succeeds silently** — and `.git` is present anyway:

```console
$ buildah build --no-cache -f Cf.keeptrue -t t-keeptrue .
STEP 2/2: ADD --keep-git-dir=true https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World.git /src
Error: building at STEP "...": ADD --keep-git-dir is not supported

$ buildah build --no-cache -f Cf.keepfalse -t t-keepfalse .
Successfully tagged localhost/t-keepfalse:latest       # <- no error, no warning

$ buildah build --no-cache -f Cf.keepnone -t t-keepnone .
Successfully tagged localhost/t-keepnone:latest

$ buildah unshare -- sh -c 'for t in t-keepfalse t-keepnone; do
    c=$(buildah from $t); m=$(buildah mount $c)
    [ -d "$m/src/.git" ] && echo "$t: .git PRESENT" || echo "$t: .git absent"
    buildah umount $c >/dev/null; buildah rm $c >/dev/null; done'
t-keepfalse: .git PRESENT
t-keepnone:  .git PRESENT
```

So `--keep-git-dir=false` produces a byte-identical result to omitting the flag entirely: the
user asked for `.git` to be dropped and got it shipped.

## Describe the results you expected

Either `/src/.git` absent, or an error stating the flag is unsupported — matching what
`--keep-git-dir=true` already does one line above.

## Root cause

**Parse** — `vendor/github.com/openshift/imagebuilder/dispatchers.go:203-206` correctly maps
all three forms:

```go
case arg == "--keep-git-dir", arg == "--keep-git-dir=true":
    keepGitDir = true
case arg == "--keep-git-dir=false":
    keepGitDir = false
```

**Enforcement** — `imagebuildah/stage_executor.go:376-382` guards only the true case:

```go
for _, cp := range copies {
    if cp.KeepGitDir {
        if cp.Download {
            return errors.New("ADD --keep-git-dir is not supported")
        }
        return errors.New("COPY --keep-git-dir is not supported")
    }
```

With `keepGitDir == false` the guard is skipped entirely and the flag has no effect anywhere
downstream.

**Behaviour** — `add.go:596-624` copies the clone wholesale with no `.git` exclusion:

```go
getErr = copier.Get(repositoryDir, repositoryDir, getOptions, []string{"."}, writer)
```

and `define.TempDirForURL` (`define/types.go:285-323`) produces the tree via
`git init` + `git fetch --depth=1` + `git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, so `.git` is present in
`repositoryDir`.

## The broader inversion

Buildah's effective default for `ADD <git-url>` is BuildKit's `--keep-git-dir=true` —
the inverse of BuildKit, where `.git` is stripped unless you ask for it.

This is load-bearing in the test suite: `tests/bud.bats:8238` runs
`git -C /podman-branch rev-parse HEAD` **inside the built image**, which only passes because
`.git` is retained. So the retention is currently asserted behaviour, not an accident — but
it is undocumented, and it means the flag that would let a user opt out is the one that
silently does nothing.

## Design context

Hard-erroring on unimplemented flags was the deliberate interim contract, per
[openshift/imagebuilder#285](https://github.com/openshift/imagebuilder/pull/285)
(merged 2024-06-22):

> Unless/until we implement logic for them, have the `dockerclient` implementation error out
> if the `--link`, `--parent`, `--keep-git-dir`, or `--excludes` flags are supplied to `ADD`
> or `COPY`.

The `=false` case falls through that contract: it is an unimplemented flag that does **not**
error out, which is precisely the outcome the contract was written to prevent.

## Suggested fix

Pick one; both are small:

1. **Consistent with the current contract** — error on `--keep-git-dir=false` too, since the
   behaviour it requests is not implemented. Simplest, and honest.

2. **Better, and closes #5916's use case in passing** — actually implement the flag. Exclude
   `.git` when `keepGitDir` is false, retain it when true, and pick a default. Note that
   flipping the default to match BuildKit (strip unless asked) would be a breaking change and
   would need `tests/bud.bats:8238` updated, so defaulting to `true` and honouring an explicit
   `false` is the conservative path.

Option 2 also unblocks the concrete request in #5916 — @lrowe, 2025-03-21:

> The `--keep-git-dir` is helpful when you want to subsequently fetch submodules with
> `git submodule update --init --recursive` which requires the `.git` directory to be present.

## Related

- #5916 — `ADD --keep-git-dir` support missing (**open since 2025-01-17, no maintainer
  response**; covers the `=true` half only — the `=false` silent-ignore is unreported)
- #4974 → #5438 — `ADD <git ref>` support (the PR that introduced the divergence). @rhatdan,
  2023-08-14, on the original request: *"If docker supports it, so should we."*
- #4453 — builds from git repo URLs don't recurse submodules (open; same submodule use case)
- openshift/imagebuilder#285 — the hard-error contract quoted above

## Environment

```
$ buildah version
Version:         1.45.0
Go Version:      go1.26.5-X:nodwarf5
Image Spec:      1.1.1
Runtime Spec:    1.3.0
image Version:   5.41.0
Git Commit:      7ae7d5a4021b24d02a5c281badca8c4d8ebbf442

$ pacman -Q buildah
buildah 1:1.45.0-1
```

Rootless, kernel 7.1.8-arch1-3.

Reproduced above on the released **1.45.0**. The source analysis was done against `main`
@ `b544ad829` (1.46.0-dev), where the same parse/enforcement mismatch is present.

comments.body:
Docker excludes the `.git` by default https://docs.docker.com/reference/dockerfile/#add---keep-git-dir and the same semantics is described by `openshift/imagebuilder` https://github.com/openshift/imagebuilder/blob/035359d69d4e679c502aa124341ae87d5bc73f56/builder.go#L44 which buildah vendors to do the parsing.

The error for `--keep-git-dir=true` originates from this commit https://github.com/podman-container-tools/buildah/commit/d6771f81afd74e4f1a4a7ad5434f63d72c253de2 and the reasoning is that it is better to error than let the user assume that the flag works. However, this is kind of unfortunate, since unlike docker, buildah does keep the `.git` by default, so on `--keep-git-dir=true` it errors even when it could fulfill the user's wish seamlessly, while on `--keep-git-dir=false`, where the error would make more sense, it cannot be emitted.

So as it is now, buildah gets a `bool`, so it cannot distinguish between `--keep-git-dir=false` and `without --keep-git-dir altogether`, so

> error on --keep-git-dir=false too, since the behaviour it requests is not implemented. Simplest, and honest.

is not that simple, as it involves either an upstream change on `openshift/imagebuilder`, or manual parsing to see if the flag is present at all.

## Options

### 1. supporting the flag, with `false` as default

This seems reasonable and it covers docker compatibility, but it would break for the users that expect the `.git` to be there even without the flag.

### 2. supporting the flag, with `true` as default

This would mean moving further away from docker, and it would require implementing the distinguishing between `--keep-git-dir` is set to false` and `--keep-git-dir is not there at all`. Keeps compatibility with current behavior.

### 3. keeping the flag unsupported, warning the user if they use it with `false`

This would consist parsing the line to see if the `--keep-git-dir=false` is there. To continue the

> rejecting the flags outright is far preferable to quietly ignoring them

idea.

### 4. remove the error on `true`, since it covers the wrong branch

It does not help the user much to see an error on `true`, when the functionality is `remove this flag and it will work`.
